status: unrefereed research candidate; internal AI-assisted review only

target.citation: Xu, Kolchinsky, Delvenne & Ito (2025), Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 257102, Supplement Eq. (S3)

claims.statement: Supplement Eq. (S3) implies that every eigenvalue lambda of an irreducible n-state rate matrix gives zeta = 1 + Re(lambda)/alpha + i Im(lambda)/(alpha beta') in the Karpelevich region Omega_n, under either reading of its quantifiers.
The integer rate matrix Q_w has eigenvalue -4745 + 450 sqrt(3) i whose rescaled image lies outside Omega_4, so (S3) is false.
Containment holds for every irreducible bidirectional rate matrix on at most three states, so four is the smallest failing dimension.
claims.dependsOn: sector bound of Ohga, Ito & Kolchinsky (2023), Eq. (10)

claims.statement: Counterexamples exist near every point of the open left boundary arc of Omega_4 (resetting family, epsilon small).
For a = 2/3, t = 14/27 every 0 < epsilon <= 1/100 gives a counterexample, and there is an open set of positive-rate counterexamples.
For every n >= 4 there are rate matrices violating containment (fix n, then t in (0, eta_n), then epsilon < epsilon_0(n,t); thresholds non-explicit).
At n = 5, t = 1/20 the radial margin becomes positive from about epsilon = e^-16.3 and the triangle dominates near e^-18 = t^6.
Whether containment holds for single-cycle networks.
claims.note: multistart search on 4- and 5-state rings found no violation; evidence only

scope: All counterexamples use the complete graph. The proved affinity ellipse and Farey-polygon bounds are unaffected.
